  • Haida↗Continuing specific community and government connection

    Continuing specific community and government connection

  • Kwakwaka'wakw↗Community cultural institution connection
    Connection & source
    Community cultural institution connection

    The Society explicitly states that it is located in Alert Bay, British Columbia, and that its mandate concerns the cultural heritage of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw. This is a direct British Columbia institutional connection. Inspection: Actual homepage introductory sentence, line 10, plus About Us mandate and society paragraphs, lines 9–17, inspected. The explicit facility location, not incorporation under provincial law alone, supplies the geographic tie. Limits: This collective name encompasses distinct communities and nations. The Society is not presented as one government for them all. No ceremonial narratives, regalia images, sales listings or permissions to reuse cultural material are adopted.

    Public institution content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Nuu-chah-nulth↗Present inter community council location
    Connection & source
    Present inter community council location

    The Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council describes its support for Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations and communities and publishes its office in Port Alberni, British Columbia. This establishes an institutional British Columbia route for the collective directory name. Inspection: Read the homepage's Vision and Mission, community-service descriptions, and council address. The mission explicitly speaks of First Nations in the plural. Limits: This initial connection is to the council's published location, not a mapped homeland, reserve extent, or statement that every Nuu-chah-nulth First Nation has one government. The council and the peoples/constituent First Nations are not interchangeable. No separate deep-profile source count is assigned to this homepage.

    Current council self-description and contact location, inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Pentlatch↗Historical community connection in nation published account
    Connection & source
    Historical community connection in nation published account

    K’ómoks First Nation’s account distinguishes Pentlatch people and language and connects their histories with the Comox Valley, Vancouver Island. Pentlatch is a related historical/community access point within a present nation’s diverse history, rather than a wholly separate present government. Inspection: Actual cultural introduction, lines 74–76, and history/timeline, particularly Comox Valley and 1876 administrative merger. Origin narratives, counts and contemporary title assertions are not adopted.

    Historical Comox Valley communities and their later relationship in K’ómoks First Nation. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Saanich↗Traditional community / cross border regional connection
    Connection & source
    Traditional community / cross border regional connection

    The Leadership Council describes W̱SÁNEĆ/Saanich villages on the Saanich Peninsula and Southern Gulf Islands in Canada and the San Juan Islands in present Washington. Its homeland account supplies the British Columbia context. Modern bands, traditional communities and the wider people are related but not identical. These are broad historical routes, not legal-title determinations. Inspection: Actual Before the reserve system paragraph, lines 28–32; separate homeland introduction, lines 89–94. No place-name geometry, sensitive sites, oral-history retelling or territorial declaration copied.

    Pre-reserve villages described in community history published May 19, 2022. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Secwepemc↗Related people names / specific council connection

    Related people names / specific council connection

    SNTC identifies its origins in Secwepemc chiefs and its work with Shuswap communities, and locates its office in Kamloops, British Columbia.
